questions.questionText: When does an object falling vertically through the air reach terminal velocity?

options.text: when the acceleration of the object becomes negative
when the acceleration of the object is equal to g
when the air resistance equals the weight of the object
when the air resistance is greater than the weight of the object

questions.questionText: Which statement about the mass and the weight of an object is correct?

options.text: They are both affected by changes in the acceleration of free fall.
Weight is calculated by dividing mass by the acceleration of free fall.

questions.questionText: Which statement about the mass of an object is correct?

options.text: It is equal to the density divided by the volume.
It is equal to weight multiplied by the gravitational field strength.
It is the effect of a gravitational field on the object.
It is the property that resists a change in velocity.
